amendments.by: founder (chat: "generally what people calculate in real world? is that views or followers....guide me and make change accordigly")
amendments.trigger: The first live production creator read 86% engagement.
amendments.findings: 165,074 was already an average, not a total (17,002,632 likes over 103 visible-like posts; a total would print 8,860%). A 30-day window only moves it to 84.6%. Her own non-collab posts alone give 60.3%, photos and carousels alone 75.0%. The cause is the divisor: 192,222 followers against 3,383,916 average reel views, about 17x her audience.
changes: Instagram engagement = (likes + comments) / views across the measured reels, matching the YouTube half of this feature. Falls back to followers when a creator posted no reels, recording the basis.
The numbers are computed from the newest 30 posts inside the 90-day window (SOCIAL_MAX_POSTS), not every post in it. Equal weight per creator.
window_start/window_end now record the span the measured posts cover, so the detail screen prints the real range.
Migration 179 adds ig_engagement_basis and posts_seen, and retires every engagement figure computed under the old rule.

Measured 2026-09-12: asking the Instagram actor for exactly N posts does NOT return the newest N (30 requested overlapped the true newest 30 by 28; 5 requested skipped four of the five newest). So the fetch still covers the whole window and the cap is applied in socialCalc, where sorting by published_at makes it exact. No Apify saving from the cap.
amendments.effect: Test creator Instagram engagement 86.0% -> 5.1%. YouTube unchanged (long 1.5%, shorts 2.5%). Apify cost unchanged.
amendments.mockup_impact: Tile label "Posts in 90 days" -> "Recent posts", "Uploads in 90 days" -> "Recent uploads", detail heading "LAST 90 DAYS" -> "RECENT POSTS"/"RECENT UPLOADS", and the Instagram formula line now states the views basis and how many posts of how many were used.
